questions.q: Why does LTV Global reject an all-at-once cutover across all regions and business units?
options: Because an all-at-once cutover would concentrate every possible failure mode into one weekend with no way to isolate which change caused which problem
Because Salesforce technically prohibits migrating more than one region at a time
Because all-at-once migrations are always more expensive than phased ones
Because dealers refuse to migrate at the same time as end customers
questions.explain: Phased waves let LTV Global isolate and address problems wave by wave, rather than risking every possible failure mode happening simultaneously with no way to trace the cause.

questions.q: Why does EMEA, with EuroCRM retirement, go first in the migration sequence rather than last?
options: Because EMEA has the least legacy debt of the three regions
Because alphabetical ordering was used to decide the sequence
Because it is the hardest, most disruption-sensitive migration, and sequencing it first puts the team's freshest attention and contingency budget against the highest-risk wave
Because GDPR legally requires EMEA to migrate before any other region
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly argues for sequencing the hardest, most disruption-sensitive migration first, while the team's attention and contingency budget are freshest, rather than saving it for last when the team may already be fatigued from earlier waves.

questions.q: How does the EuroCRM parallel-run period resolve Risk #5 from the Chapter 1 risk register?
options: By deleting EuroCRM immediately once Salesforce go-live begins
By letting technicians keep operating in EuroCRM alongside the new Salesforce functionality during a defined window, giving a fallback if the new process reveals a gap
By migrating EuroCRM data without any testing
By skipping EMEA's migration entirely
questions.explain: The parallel-run period is the specific mechanism resolving the risk of EuroCRM's cutover disrupting EMEA field service — technicians have a working fallback while any gaps in the new process get fixed, rather than facing a hard cutover with no safety net.

questions.q: Why does APAC's migration wave come last, per this lesson?
options: Because APAC has the most legacy debt of any region
Because APAC does not use any Salesforce functionality
Because APAC's leadership refused to participate in the project
Because APAC has the least legacy debt, making its rollout closer to a clean deployment than a true migration, and it benefits from lessons learned in the earlier waves
questions.explain: APAC, as LTV Global's newest and fastest-growing region, has comparatively little legacy debt to migrate away from, and going last lets it benefit from what was learned migrating EMEA and North America first.

questions.q: What happens to EuroCRM's service-history and contact data during the migration, per this lesson?
options: It is extracted, cleansed, mapped onto the Service Contract and Case data model, and loaded before the parallel-run period begins
It is discarded, since EuroCRM is being retired anyway
It is migrated directly into LedgerPoint instead of Salesforce
It remains in EuroCRM permanently and is never migrated
questions.explain: Because this data exists nowhere else in the landscape (per Lesson 4), it goes through a dedicated data-migration workstream — extracted, cleansed, mapped, and loaded before parallel-run begins — so technicians see real historical context in the new system.
